subject: humanities
passage: The first part of Miguel de Cervantes's Don Quixote, published in Madrid in 1605, was so popular that readers waited impatiently for more adventures of the deluded knight and his practical squire, Sancho Panza. Cervantes, who was nearly sixty when the first part appeared, worked slowly on a continuation. Another writer, however, moved faster than Cervantes did. Stung by the appearance in 1614 of an unauthorized sequel written under the name Alonso Fernández de Avellaneda, whose true identity remains unknown, ______ Some scholars suspect that the insult hurried Cervantes to finish the book.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: Cervantes's genuine second part, published in 1615, openly mocks the impostor, even letting Don Quixote meet a character from the false book.
choices.B: the genuine second part, which Cervantes published in 1615, openly mocks the impostor, even letting Don Quixote meet a character from the false book.
choices.C: Cervantes openly mocked the impostor in his own second part, published in 1615, even letting Don Quixote meet a character from the false book.
choices.D: mockery of the impostor fills the genuine second part that Cervantes published in 1615, which even lets Don Quixote meet a character from the false book.

explanation.why: The introductory phrase "Stung by the appearance in 1614 of an unauthorized sequel" describes a person who felt insulted: Cervantes. A modifier at the start of a sentence applies to the subject that comes right after the comma, so that subject must be Cervantes himself, not his book.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The subject is "second part"; "Cervantes's" only describes the book, so the sentence says the book was stung.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This makes "the genuine second part" the subject, so the sentence says the book was stung by the sequel.
explanation.C: Correct. "Cervantes" comes right after the introductory phrase, so it is clear that he is the one who was stung.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This makes "mockery" the subject, so the sentence says the mockery was stung by the sequel.
